title: Production deployment failed due to missing environment variable
description: During the v2.4.0 release, the deployment to production failed because the DATABASE_POOL_SIZE environment variable was not propagated to the new Kubernetes namespace. Service was down for 23 minutes before rollback completed. Lesson learned: add a pre-deployment validation step that checks all required environment variables are present in the target namespace before promoting the build.
creator: amanda.chen@example.com

title: Customer data export job silently truncated large result sets
description: A scheduled customer data export job was silently capping output at 10,000 rows due to an undocumented default limit in the reporting library. The issue went unnoticed for three weeks until a finance auditor flagged inconsistent totals. Lesson learned: any batch job producing variable-size outputs must log both the input row count and the output row count, and alert when they diverge.
creator: raj.patel@example.com

title: Hardcoded API key leaked in public commit
description: A developer accidentally committed a third-party billing API key to a public branch while debugging locally. The key was detected by an external scanner within 40 minutes and the vendor auto-revoked it, but not before two unauthorized API calls were made. Lesson learned: enforce pre-commit secret scanning hooks on every developer workstation and require all third-party keys to be loaded from the secrets manager, never hardcoded even temporarily.
creator: lena.fischer@example.com

title: Stale feature flag caused confusing UI behavior in QA
description: A feature flag left enabled in the QA environment six months after the feature shipped caused testers to file duplicate bugs about an old experimental layout. Investigation took two days because the flag's owner had left the company. Lesson learned: every feature flag must have a documented owner and an expiration date; flags older than 90 days post-launch should be auto-flagged for cleanup.
creator: marcus.webb@example.com

title: Database failover did not promote read replica as expected
description: A planned failover drill revealed that the read replica had silently fallen out of sync three weeks earlier due to a replication slot conflict, so promotion produced stale data. Lesson learned: replication lag must be monitored with alerts at both warning and critical thresholds, and failover drills must be run quarterly rather than annually.
creator: sofia.alvarez@example.com

title: CI pipeline cache poisoning slowed every build for a week
description: A corrupted node_modules cache from a flaky build was promoted to the shared cache key, causing every downstream build to install broken dependencies. Builds took 3x longer for a week before someone manually invalidated the cache. Lesson learned: cache keys should include a content hash of the lockfile, and any failed build must skip cache promotion.
creator: kenji.tanaka@example.com

title: Vendor SaaS outage exposed lack of fallback plan
description: When our identity provider had a 90-minute regional outage, downstream services that relied on JWT verification began rejecting all requests because the JWKS endpoint was unreachable and we had no local cache. Lesson learned: cache JWKS keys locally with a sensible TTL, and treat any third-party dependency without a documented degradation mode as a P1 architectural risk.
creator: priya.nair@example.com

title: Onboarding doc referenced decommissioned VPN gateway
description: Three new hires lost half a day each trying to connect through a VPN gateway that had been decommissioned eight months earlier but was still listed as the primary entry point in the onboarding wiki. Lesson learned: any infrastructure decommission must include a checklist item to update onboarding documentation, and the onboarding doc should have a quarterly review owner.
creator: tom.becker@example.com

title: Memory leak in image processing service caused weekly crashes
description: The image processing worker leaked roughly 200MB per day because thumbnails were cached in an unbounded in-memory dictionary keyed by URL. Pods were OOM-killed weekly, masking the issue under normal restart noise. Lesson learned: any in-memory cache must use a bounded LRU or TTL policy, and OOM kill events should trigger an alert distinct from regular pod restarts.
creator: elena.rossi@example.com

title: Flaky integration test hid a real concurrency bug for months
description: An integration test was marked flaky and retried up to five times, but the underlying failure was actually a real race condition in the order-processing module. The bug eventually surfaced in production as duplicate charges. Lesson learned: never blanket-retry tests as a flakiness mitigation; quarantine and root-cause them, and require a written explanation before merging any retry-count change.
creator: david.okafor@example.com

title: Backup restore drill revealed unrecoverable customer data
description: A scheduled restore drill found that nightly backups for the customer-attachments bucket had been silently failing for 11 days due to expired IAM credentials. Roughly 4,200 uploads from that window were unrecoverable. Lesson learned: backup jobs must publish success heartbeats to a monitoring system, and absence of a heartbeat must page within one cycle, not be detected only at restore time.
creator: hana.kim@example.com

title: Architecture decision record contradicted current implementation
description: An ADR from 2024 stated that all services would use gRPC for internal communication, but the actual fleet had drifted to a mix of REST and gRPC with no record of why. New hires designed services against the outdated ADR and had to rework them. Lesson learned: ADRs must be marked superseded with a link to the replacement when reality diverges, and a quarterly review should reconcile ADRs against the service catalog.
creator: felix.brandt@example.com

title: Timezone handling caused scheduled reports to arrive a day late
description: A reporting service used the server's local timezone instead of UTC when computing daily report cutoffs. After a datacenter region change, executive reports began arriving one day late for stakeholders in two timezones. Lesson learned: all scheduled jobs must operate in UTC internally and convert to user-facing timezones only at presentation time; timezone assumptions should be covered by explicit unit tests.
creator: natalie.cooper@example.com

title: Rate limiter misconfiguration blocked legitimate mobile traffic
description: A new rate-limit rule meant to throttle a scraping bot was applied at the wrong CIDR scope and ended up blocking all mobile users behind a major carrier's NAT for 70 minutes. Lesson learned: rate-limit changes must be tested in staging with traffic mirroring, rolled out behind a percentage flag, and reviewed by someone other than the author before applying to production.
creator: yusuf.adeyemi@example.com

title: Privilege escalation possible via stale admin role assignment
description: A security audit found that a former contractor's account retained an admin role in the analytics platform for four months after offboarding because role removal relied on a manual ticket that was never filed. Lesson learned: offboarding must trigger an automated revocation sweep across all integrated systems, and a quarterly access review must reconcile active roles against the HR roster.
creator: isabella.mendez@example.com

title: Postmortem action items went unowned and undelivered
description: A review of last year's postmortems found that 38% of action items had no owner and 60% of those that did were never closed. Several recurring incidents traced back to action items from prior outages that had been quietly abandoned. Lesson learned: every postmortem action item must have a single named owner, a due date, and be tracked in the same backlog as feature work, with monthly review by engineering leadership.
creator: ravi.subramanian@example.com

title: Dependabot PRs piled up unreviewed for nine months
description: A peripheral repository accumulated 140 unreviewed Dependabot PRs because the CODEOWNERS file pointed to a team that had been reorganized away. When a CVE finally forced attention, the upgrade path was a multi-week project instead of a routine bump. Lesson learned: CODEOWNERS files must be validated against current org membership in CI, and any repo with more than 20 open dependency PRs should trigger an alert.
creator: claire.dubois@example.com

title: Load test environment did not match production network topology
description: A capacity load test predicted comfortable headroom, but a real traffic spike saturated an internal NAT gateway that did not exist in the load test environment. Lesson learned: load test environments must mirror production network topology including NAT, egress proxies, and inter-AZ links, and any topology drift must be tracked as a known risk in the test report.
creator: oliver.shah@example.com

title: Email notifications batched incorrectly during incident
description: During a Sev-2 incident, the on-call notification system batched alerts on a 15-minute interval, so the responder did not see escalating symptoms until well after the customer impact began. Lesson learned: incident-class notifications must bypass batching entirely, and notification routing rules should be reviewed as part of every quarterly incident response drill.
creator: amir.khan@example.com

title: Disaster recovery runbook contained outdated console URLs
description: During a regional cloud provider degradation, responders followed the documented DR runbook only to find that three of the listed admin console URLs pointed to a deprecated portal that had been retired in a vendor migration. The team improvised and recovered, but RTO targets were missed by 40 minutes. Lesson learned: DR runbooks must be exercised end-to-end at least twice a year with a real responder following the doc verbatim, and any deviation must trigger an immediate runbook update.
creator: grace.holloway@example.com
